title: Reserve Oversight Operator Panel — compact controls for dedicated capacity health, autoscale and burst
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Design a compact operator panel for Dedicated capacity owners that surfaces GPU pool health, predictive autoscale suggestions, and one-click burst controls. The goal is a single, embeddable panel (mini-dashboard) that SREs and platform engineers can add to their reserve overview, mobile/compact console view, and incident runbooks. Key themes: rapid triage, low surface area config changes, preflight simulations for burst windows, and clear rollback lanes.
acceptance_criteria: Panel implemented as a reusable console component and added to Dedicated pool detail page
Displays real-time SLO indicators (p99 latency, error rate) and predicted 15m surge risk
Provides a compact autoscale composer: target utilization slider + smart-preview of impact on token latency and cost
Burst controls allow pre-authorized temporary capacity increases with a simulated cost preview and automatic rollback timer
Keyboard accessible and passes WCAG AA color contrast for all critical indicators
Design handoff includes component tokens, interaction specs, and two edge-case flows (node loss, quota exhausted)
design_notes: We explored three layout densities: full canvas, mid-card, and micro-panel. The micro-panel won for the initial release because it fits sidebars and runbook embeds with minimal cognitive load. New visual primitives: 'health fingerprint' (radial condensed SLO summary), 'burst-lattice' (compact timeline showing scheduled bursts vs predicted load), and 'throttle rail' (vertical slider for target util). Prototype in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/reserve-oversight-panel. High-fidelity screens include dark/light tokens and a compact mobile breakpoint. Interaction flows include: 1) Preflight simulation modal, 2) Authorize burst (with 2FA confirm for customers with stricter policies), 3) Rollback suggestion after burst ends. We intentionally avoid configurable autoscale policies in the micro-panel — those remain in the detailed pool settings to reduce risk of accidental global changes.
decisions: Ship micro-panel variant first; full canvas deferred to Q3
Expose only safe controls: target utilization slider, burst window scheduler, and cancel/rollback; no direct node-level patching in panel
Include simulated cost preview for every burst action to reduce surprise billing complaints
Add a lightweight audit trail link pointing to Private KMS/audit logs for enterprise customers (link to audit page)
